summary:
The Last Signal is an interactive educational project based on NASA's Mars Exploration Rover Mission and the journey of its twin rovers, Spirit and Opportunity. It brings their remarkable story to life through a four-chapter narrative, covering their construction, exploration of Mars, scientific discoveries, challenges, and eventual loss of communication with Earth.

The project features an interactive website with engaging visuals, chapter-based storytelling, mission timelines, and a multiple-choice quiz to test users' understanding. It combines real scientific events with creative storytelling to make space exploration more accessible and interesting.

The main goal is to make learning about Mars more engaging than simply presenting scientific facts. Through this project, users can understand how scientists study other planets, recognize evidence of ancient water on Mars, and learn how robotic missions contribute to space research. It also highlights how Spirit and Opportunity continued operating far beyond their planned 90-day missions, demonstrating the value of persistence and scientific exploration.
details:
The Mars Files is an interactive website that explores the missions and discoveries of NASA’s Mars Exploration Rovers, Spirit and Opportunity. It presents their journeys through an engaging, space-themed experience, allowing visitors to explore the rovers, follow their timelines, read their stories, view NASA photographs, and learn about the scientific discoveries they made on Mars. The website also includes audio narration and a final quiz to make learning more interactive.

The main benefit of this project is that it makes space science easier and more interesting to understand, especially for students and young space enthusiasts. Instead of presenting information through lengthy articles, it uses storytelling, images, timelines, and interactive features to help visitors learn at their own pace.

The intended impact is to increase awareness of NASA’s Mars exploration missions and help people understand the importance of the discoveries made by Spirit and Opportunity. Their findings provided evidence that Mars once had liquid water and may have had conditions suitable for microbial life. Through this project, we hope to inspire curiosity about space exploration and encourage more young people to take an interest in science and technology.

The website was developed using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. HTML was used to structure the content, CSS to design the space-themed interface, and JavaScript to create interactive features such as rover selection, story navigation, and the quiz. NASA photographs and information from official NASA sources were also used to support the content.

The creative aspect of the project is its space-museum and investigative storytelling approach. Visitors are not simply reading about the missions; they are exploring the information as if they were investigating a collection of Mars mission records. Features such as the interactive rover archive, scrolling timeline, audio narration, and quiz make the experience more engaging.

While developing the project, our team considered the intended audience, accuracy of scientific information, ease of navigation, visual design, and accessibility. We also considered how to present complex scientific discoveries in simple language without losing their importance. Our goal was to create an educational experience that is informative, interactive, and enjoyable.
